episodes.189943: Clusters of strong thunderstorms with gusty winds and hail during the late morning and midday hours and spread west to east across north Alabama.
episodes.189949: A surface low over West Tennessee triggered the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms across northwestern Central Alabama during the afternoon of May 18. This activity moved southeastward through the evening hours, occasionally producing hail and pockets of wind damage. Eastern Autauga County and southwestern Elmore County were most affected, with numerous downed trees and power outages from Pine Level to Millbrook.
episodes.190203: A cold front moving northwest to southeast helped support strong to severe storms that mainly generated high winds, with a peak wind gust of 90 mph at the Grand River Remote Automatic Weather Station (RAWS)  situated 11 miles south of the community of Bullhead. Additional wind gust resulted in damage to grain bins and power poles 2 miles north northwest of, and 3 miles northwest of Sand Lake Wildlife Refuge respectively. Shingle damage was reported at a residence 2 miles east of Eureka and thunderstorm winds also resulted in local brownout conditions 8 miles east northeast of Frederick.
episodes.190248: Strong storms with gusty winds of 35-45 kts moved offshore of the local Atlantic coast in the afternoon ahead of a cold front.
episodes.190696: Severe Wind was observed with a QLCS moving through the central Red River Valley on the evening of May 17th.
episodes.190700: Severe Wind was observed with a QLCS moving through the central Red River Valley into northwestern Minnesota on the evening of May 17th.
episodes.190833: An upper level trough passed across the central Appalachians during the afternoon and evening of May 18th, triggering widely scattered showers and thunderstorms to the north of a stationary front stretching across northern North Carolina.  Upper level winds ahead of the trough were light.  Moisture was abundant, with precipitable water values ranging from 1.2 to 1.3 inches across southeast West Virginia, while surface dewpoint temperatures were observed in the mid 60s.  Mixed Layer CAPE (Convective Available Potential Energy) was in excess of 1,000 J/Kg during the afternoon and evening.  The thunderstorms that developed during the afternoon and evening were localized but extremely efficient at producing rainfall, with rates within several storms exceeding four inches per hour.  They were also slow-moving, allowing the storms to remain over locations for extended periods of time.||In the Town of Bluewell, heavy rain began falling at around 6:30 PM EDT and continued through around 8:30 PM EDT before exiting the area.  Rainfall rates were estimated to be between three and four inches per hour, with a radar-estimated total of nearly four inches.  By 8:40 pm EDT, CREST Unit Streamflows had risen to over 540 cfs/mi^2 in the Bluewell area, with the FLASH 3-hour average recurrence interval indicating a 200+-year event.  The 3-hour QPE/FFG ratio over the town indicated that rainfall was between 2 and 2.25 times that of the 3-hour flash flood guidance.  Some of the more flood-prone areas around Bluewell experienced flash flooding, including along Airport Road and Coal Heritage Road, which have been noted to experience flooding in the past.
episodes.190879: A severe thunderstorm developed over western Fall River County and tracked eastward into Oglala Lakota County. The storm produced wind gusts to around 70 mph along its path.
episodes.190882: A thunderstorm became severe over northern Jackson and southern Haakon counties for a brief period, producing wind gusts to around 60 mph.
episodes.190886: A cluster of thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon on Saturday (5/18) and tracked through central and north-central Wisconsin during the late afternoon and evening hours. The strongest storms produced large hail up to golf ball size and gusty winds.
episodes.190959: A training line of thunderstorms occurred just west of South Boston, producing between three and four inches of rainfall within a span of three hours.  Rainfall rates at times were observed to be in excess of 3.5 inches per hour.  Runoff from this rainfall collected in Poplar Creek, causing the creek to rise out of its banks in the town of South Boston, resulting in flooding of roads near the Dan River.  FLASH data did not appear impressive with this event, indicating a maximum 1-hou ARI of between a 10-year and a 20-year event.  The 1-hour QPE/FFG ration maxed out at 1.0, and CREST Unit Streamflow was marginal, between 90 and 180 cfs/mi^2.
episodes.190977: An upper level trough passed across the central Appalachians during the afternoon and evening of May 18th, triggering widely scattered showers and thunderstorms to the north of a stationary front stretching across northern North Carolina.  Upper level winds ahead of the trough were light.  Moisture was abundant, with precipitable water values ranging from 1.2 to 1.3 inches across northwest North Carolina, while surface dewpoint temperatures were observed in the mid to upper 60s.  Mixed Layer CAPE (Convective Available Potential Energy) values observed during the afternoon and evening were in excess of 1,000 J/Kg.  The thunderstorms that developed during the afternoon and evening were localized but extremely efficient at producing rainfall, with rates within several storms exceeding four inches per hour.  They were also slow-moving, allowing the storms to remain over locations for extended periods of time.
episodes.190984: A severe thunderstorm developed over northeast Campbell County, then tracked into Crook County before dissipating. The storm produced large hail to around quarter size near Oshoto.
episodes.191162: An upper level disturbance tracked across the Ohio Valley and brought showers and storms into the area on May 17th. Stratiform rain fell across the area during the first half of the day, then storms began to develop and train across southeast Ohio during the evening. These storms deposited one and a half to two inches of rain over Jackson County, causing flash flooding to occur along a couple of roads within the county. Precipitation departed and brought an end to flooding later that night.
episodes.191197: A dust devil injured one person in Las Vegas.
episodes.191240: Scattered storms formed across portions of western Wisconsin during the late afternoon of May 18th and moved east into central Wisconsin throughout the evening. These storms produced large hail with several reports up to 2 inches in diameter, especially across portions of Clark, Taylor, Jackson and Trempealeau counties.
episodes.191308: Storms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts along the coast and across the local Atlantic waters.
episodes.191309: A strong thunderstorm produced wind damage in Lake County.
episodes.191358: A weak but slow moving upper trough a severe thunderstorm that produced a few instances of damaging winds.
episodes.191401: Thunderstorms developed across northwestern Wisconsin during the afternoon hours of the 18th ahead of a cold front and an incoming upper level shortwave. Conditions were favorable for large hail and gusty winds in the region and a few of the storms were able to produce severe hail as they moved through. The largest hail reported was to the size of ping pong balls north of Mercer during the mid-afternoon.
episodes.191547: Another period of active weather ensued from the May 13th through the 17th. During this time, rounds of showers and thunderstorms moved across the state. Heavy rains brought flash flooding to some locations.
episodes.191620: An upper level short-wave trough and a cold front pushed through western and central North Dakota resulting in thunderstorms developing by mid-afternoon. The main threat from these storms was damaging wind gusts, but a few storms produced large hail. The strongest reported wind gust of 70 mph occurred at the Hettinger Airport in Adams County, while the largest hail reported was the size of a half-dollar, which occurred near Burt in Hettinger County.
episodes.191668: A passing shortwave trough created areas of showers over southwest Pennsylvania during the morning of May 18th. Localized low-level convergence led to radar-estimated rain totals of 1.5 to 2.5 inches over portions of Allegheny County, creating some issues with road flooding.
episodes.191767: A stalled frontal boundary was draped across northern North Carolina. Increasing dew points and strong surface heating along and just south of the boundary aided in increasing instability by the afternoon hours. Storms developed along the stalled boundary and produced a few instances of damaging winds.
episodes.191786: A stalled frontal boundary was draped across northern North Carolina and near southern and central Virginia. Increasing dew points and strong surface heating along and just south of the boundary aided in increasing instability by the afternoon hours. Storms developed along the stalled boundary and produced a few instances of damaging winds.
episodes.191802: Thunderstorms developed over the mountains of northern Mexico. One of these storms produced large hail in Edwards County.
episodes.191823: A decaying MCV crept into the Mid-South in the early hours of the morning. The MCV packed a slight punch as it took a southward dive and brought gusty and damaging winds to the area. Radar imagery depicted microburst activity resulting in some downed trees.
episodes.191824: A decaying MCV crept into the Mid-South in the early hours of the morning. The MCV packed a slight punch as it took a southward dive and brought gusty and damaging winds to the area. Radar imagery depicted microburst activity resulting in some downed trees.
episodes.191880: Minor river flooding affected portions of the Black and Cache Rivers.
episodes.191901: As an upper-level trough moved over the Florida Peninsula, abundant low-level moisture and diurnal heating led to plenty of instability in the atmosphere on May 18th. Numerous showers and thunderstorms formed in the afternoon and evening across South Florida and over the local Atlantic waters.
episodes.191902: As an upper-level trough moved over the Florida Peninsula, abundant low-level moisture and diurnal heating led to plenty of instability in the atmosphere on May 18th. Numerous showers and thunderstorms formed in the afternoon and evening across South Florida, with severe thunderstorms observed across Palm Beach County.
episodes.191961: During the early morning hours of May 17th, a long lived derecho that impacted the north central Gulf coast clipped portions of Gulf and Franklin counties with significant wind gusts in excess of hurricane force measured, along with impacts to trees and power lines and minor structural damage. Later in the day and on May 18th, additional rounds of severe storms impacted the tri-state area with damage to trees and power lines.
episodes.191962: During the early morning hours of May 17th, a long lived derecho that impacted the north central Gulf coast clipped portions of Gulf and Franklin counties with significant wind gusts in excess of hurricane force measured, along with impacts to trees and power lines and minor structural damage. Later in the day and on May 18th, additional rounds of severe storms impacted the tri-state area with damage to trees and power lines.
episodes.191963: During the early morning hours of May 17th, a long lived derecho that impacted the north central Gulf coast clipped portions of Gulf and Franklin counties with significant wind gusts in excess of hurricane force measured, along with impacts to trees and power lines and minor structural damage. Later in the day and on May 18th, additional rounds of severe storms impacted the tri-state area with damage to trees and power lines.
episodes.192016: A man was injured when lightning struck his boat off of Cape Canaveral.
episodes.192046: A cold front moving through a warm and unstable air mass generated severe thunderstorms with large hail over west half portions of Upper Michigan on the evening of the 18th.
episodes.192176: A few thunderstorms developed across western Wisconsin in the afternoon of May 18, 2024. A couple thunderstorms produced severe hail in Chippewa and Eau Claire counties. The largest hail was quarter to ping pong ball size.
episodes.192207: A weak surface trough over the area helped trigger convection over southwestern Virginia.
episodes.192271: Strong thunderstorms triggered by the progressive flow aloft initiated off the coast of Louisiana during the early morning hours. One particular storm produced a strong wind gust near the mouth of the Mississippi River. This activity continued for a few more hours before the marine instability decreased during the late morning.
episodes.192360: Scattered, slow-moving thunderstorms developed across the mountains and foothills of North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. One of the storms developed over the city of Marion and produced flash flooding.
episodes.192622: Strong thunderstorms over the marine waters adjacent to Florida produced strong wind gusts.

Rainfall rates in the strongest cells ranged anywhere from three to locally five inches per hour.  Runoff from the rainfall caused flooding across multiple roads along Highway 67 between the communities of East Bend and Jonesville.  In the area surrounding the community of East Bend, Chestnut Street was flooded and impassible due to heavy runoff. Trout Run Road was flooded and impassible due to Trout Run overflowing its banks several inches deep across the road.  A slow-moving thunderstorm produced between 2.5 and 3.5 inches of rainfall within most of the Trout Run watershed during a 60 to 75 minute period, or in excess of a 100-year Average Recurrence Interval for a 1-hour duration per MRMS FLASH.  The 1-hour QPE to FFG ratio was close to a 3, or nearly 3 times the 1-hour rainfall needed to produce flash flooding.  CREST Unit Streamflow indicated flows in the upper part of the basin reaching around 700 cfs/mi^2, a strong indicator of flash flooding.
